provenance: Telephone call, 2026-09-03, Larry's son asking the tier-1 questions from the interview guide and typing Larry's answers as he spoke them. The Camp Zama date question had been promoted to the head of the guide that morning. Raw capture: research/interviews/breakfast-questions.md, annotated in place under each question.
text: It was already there when I got to Vietnam. After the CBC people. After the rocket launch.
researchNotes: CONFIRMS THE HYPOTHESIS RAISED THE SAME DAY AND RESETS THE SEARCH. Asked plainly whether he saw the helicopter come down or whether it was already there, he answered that it was already there when he arrived in Vietnam. The archive had swept the VHPA and DIA loss records for his whole tour, found no loss at Nui Ba Den or in Tay Ninh province, and then reasoned that the wreck might predate him because he never claimed to have seen it fall and did not know whose aircraft it was. That reasoning is now confirmed by him. The search window for issue #89 moves to BEFORE September 1964, and his "7 guys dead, burnt for 3 hours" is what he was told rather than what he witnessed. The second and third sentences - "After the CBC people. After the rocket launch." - answer the separate relative-dating question about when the PHOTOGRAPH was taken, and are not in conflict with the wreck predating him.
